Frances Burney.bio: Novelist and diarist. Author of Evelina, Cecilia, Camilla, The Wanderer. Keeper of the Robes to Queen Charlotte 1786-91. Married Alexandre d'Arblay 1793.

Charles Burney Sr.bio: Musicologist, organist, Fellow of the Royal Society. Author of A General History of Music. Father of Frances Burney.

Charles Burney Jr.bio: Classical scholar, schoolmaster, DD. Son of Charles Burney Sr. Greek scholar at Cambridge.

Susanna Burney Phillips.bio: Frances Burney's favourite sister. Married Captain Molesworth Phillips 1782. Died in Ireland.

Esther Burney.bio: Eldest Burney daughter. Married her cousin Charles Rousseau Burney.

Charlotte Broome.bio: Burney sister. Married (1) Clement Francis 1786, (2) Ralph Broome 1798. Mother of Charlotte Barrett.

Charlotte Barrett.bio: Frances Burney's niece. Edited and published the first edition of the Diary and Letters (1842-46).

James Burney.bio: Rear-Admiral (retired list, Jul 1821). Sailed as merchant seaman to India (incl. Bombay) 1770-71. Second lt on Cook's 2nd voyage (Adventure, 1772-74); first lt on 3rd voyage (Discovery, 1776-80), visiting Macao/Canton Dec 1779. Taught Omai English and introduced him to Banks and George III. Captain of HMS Bristol 1782; Battle of Cuddalore 20 Jun 1783 under Hughes. Disobeyed orders 1782; republican politics ended naval career. FRS 1809. Author: Chronological History of the Discoveries in the South Sea (5 vols, 1803-17); North-Eastern Voyages of Discovery (1819). Close friend of Charles Lamb. Biography: G.E. Manwaring, My Friend the Admiral (1931).

Alexandre d'Arblay.bio: French artillery officer, émigré. Married Frances Burney 1793. Served under Lafayette, then Napoleon.

Alexander d'Arblay.bio: Son of Frances Burney and Alexandre. Cambridge student. Ordained 1818.

Charles Parr Burney.bio: Son of Charles Burney Jr. Clergyman, Archdeacon of Colchester. Bought books at his grandfather's auction.

Sarah Harriet Burney.bio: Half-sister of Frances. Novelist in her own right.

Maria Allen Rishton.bio: Step-sister. Daughter of Elizabeth Allen (Charles Burney's second wife). Prolific early correspondent of Frances.

Samuel Johnson.bio: Lexicographer, essayist, poet. Author of the Dictionary. Central figure of London literary life.

Hester Thrale Piozzi.bio: Writer, salon hostess at Streatham Park. Married (1) Henry Thrale, (2) Gabriel Piozzi 1784. 'Once dearest friend' of Frances Burney.

James Boswell.bio: Biographer of Johnson. Author of the Life of Samuel Johnson (1791).

Joshua Reynolds.bio: Portrait painter, first President of the Royal Academy. Founding member of The Club with Johnson.

Henry Thrale.bio: Brewer, MP for Southwark. Husband of Hester. Host of the Streatham Park literary circle.

Hester Maria Thrale (Lady Keith).bio: Eldest Thrale daughter ('Queeney'). Married Admiral Viscount Keith 1808. Sided against her mother over the Piozzi marriage.

Susanna Arabella Thrale.bio: Fourth surviving Thrale daughter. Unmarried. Died in Kent, buried at Streatham.

Sophia Thrale Hoare.bio: Third surviving Thrale daughter. Married Henry Merrik Hoare.

Penelope Pennington.bio: Piozzi's closest female friend. 164 letters in our data. Also appears in Mary Hays's biographical index (radical feminist circle).

Samuel Crisp.bio: Frances Burney's 'Daddy Crisp'. Lived at Chessington Hall, Surrey. Failed dramatist, beloved mentor.

David Garrick.bio: Actor-manager, Drury Lane Theatre. Furnished Burney with letters of introduction for the 1770 Italian tour.

Georgiana Waddington.bio: Née Port. Granddaughter of Mary Delany. Correspondent of Frances from Wales.

Frederica Locke.bio: Of Norbury Park, Mickleham, Surrey. One of Frances Burney's closest friends.

Edmund Burke.bio: Statesman, philosopher. Author of Reflections on the Revolution in France. Led the Hastings impeachment.

Horace Walpole.bio: 4th Earl of Orford. Author, antiquarian, founder of Strawberry Hill. Son of PM Robert Walpole.

William Windham.bio: Politician, Secretary at War. Connected to both Burke and the Burney circle.

Frances Crewe.bio: Née Greville. Whig political hostess. Bridge between Burke's political world and Burney's literary one.

Queen Charlotte.bio: Queen consort of George III. Frances Burney served as her Keeper of the Robes 1786-91.

Princess Sophia.bio: Daughter of George III. 181 letters with Frances Burney — an intense late friendship.

Princess Elizabeth.bio: Daughter of George III. Married Landgrave of Hesse-Homburg 1818.

Princess Mary.bio: Daughter of George III. Married Duke of Gloucester 1816.

Padre Martini.bio: Giovanni Battista Martini. Franciscan friar, music theorist at Bologna. Taught the young Mozart. Burney's key Italian Catholic contact.

Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart.bio: Composer. Burney met the 14-year-old Mozart in Bologna, August 1770.

Leopold Mozart.bio: Musician, father of Wolfgang. Met Burney in Bologna 1770.

Johann Christian Bach.bio: The 'London Bach'. J.S. Bach's youngest son. 33 letters with Padre Martini. Lived in London from 1762.

Carl Philipp Emanuel Bach.bio: J.S. Bach's second son. Keyboard virtuoso at Hamburg. Burney spent 'many happy hours' with him, October 1772.

Christoph Willibald Gluck.bio: Opera reformer. Met Burney in Vienna 1772.

Pietro Metastasio.bio: Imperial court poet and librettist in Vienna. Met Burney 1772.

Carlo Broschi Farinelli.bio: Most famous castrato of the century. Retired to Bologna. Met Burney August 1770.

Baldassare Galuppi.bio: Venetian opera and keyboard composer. 'Had more influence on English music than any other Italian composer.' Met Burney 1770.

Giovanni Battista Sammartini.bio: Milanese symphonist, pioneer of the classical style. Met Burney July 1770.

Laura Bassi.bio: First woman to hold a university chair in Europe. Professor of physics at University of Bologna. Met Burney August 1770.

Voltaire.bio: Philosopher, writer. Burney visited him at Ferney, June 1770.

Denis Diderot.bio: Philosopher, editor of the Encyclopédie. 8 letters with Burney.

Baron d'Holbach.bio: Philosopher, salon host. His salon on rue Royale Saint-Roch was 'the Cafe d'Europe'.

Jean-Jacques Rousseau.bio: Philosopher. Burney met him in Paris on the return visit, December 1770.

Madame de Stael.bio: Germaine de Stael. Writer, salon hostess. Part of the Juniper Hall émigré circle near the d'Arblays.

Jacques-Pierre Brissot.bio: Future Girondin revolutionary leader. 4 letters with Burney in the Fonds Brissot. Guillotined.

Marie de Maisonneuve.bio: French correspondent. 172 letters with Frances Burney — major post-1802 connection.

Thomas Twining.bio: Theologian, musician, rector of Fordham, Essex. Charles Burney's closest intellectual friend. 319 letters.

William Bewley.bio: Apothecary at Great Massingham, Norfolk. Burney's trusted literary advisor. Met at King's Lynn.

Thomas Gray.bio: Poet, author of 'Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard'. Had recommended the idea of a music history to Burney. Walpole's closest correspondent.

Frederick the Great.bio: King of Prussia. Flautist and composer. Burney attended his court at Potsdam, heard him perform, October 1772.

Sir William Hamilton.bio: British envoy to Naples. Antiquarian, volcanologist. Helped Burney access Royal Museum at Portici and arranged musical introductions. Later famous for wife Emma and Nelson affair.

Joseph Priestley.bio: Chemist, theologian, Dissenter. Lunar Society member. Broke with Burke over the French Revolution.

Fulke Greville.bio: Met Burney at King's Lynn. Instrumental in bringing him back to London.

Dr. Brocklesby.bio: Richard Brocklesby. Physician. Attended Samuel Johnson in his final illness. Also physician to Edmund Burke. Fellow of the Royal Society. Bridge between Johnson and Burke networks.

Abbé Arnaud.bio: Former director of the Opéra Comique, Paris. Met Burney June 1770.

Jean Monet.bio: Connected to Paris theatre world. Met Burney 1770.

William Herschel.bio: Astronomer, discovered Uranus. Musical connection to Burney — both musicians turned scientists.

William Mason.bio: Poet, garden designer. Burney wrote to him before the 1770 tour. Also Walpole correspondent.

George Montagu.bio: Walpole's most prolific correspondent (252 letters in our data).

Henry Seymour Conway.bio: Soldier, politician. Walpole's cousin and major correspondent (139 letters).

William Cole.bio: Antiquary, clergyman. Walpole's second most frequent correspondent (161 letters).

Lord Stormont.bio: David Murray, 7th Viscount Stormont. British ambassador to Austria. Facilitated Burney's introductions in Vienna 1772.

Louis Devisme.bio: British plenipotentiary in Munich. 'Of the greatest assistance' to Burney, esp. accessing the Elector's library.

John Osborn.bio: British Envoy at Dresden. Introduced Burney to the Elector.

Gaetano Guadagni.bio: Famous castrato. Created the role of Orfeo for Gluck. Met Burney in Munich 1772.

Regina Mingotti.bio: Retired opera singer. Met Burney in Munich 1772.

Nicola Jommelli.bio: Opera composer. Met Burney in Naples 1770. Catholic.

Niccolo Piccinni.bio: Opera composer, later embroiled in the Gluck-Piccinni war in Paris. Met Burney in Naples 1770.

Giovanni Paisiello.bio: Neapolitan opera composer. Active when Burney visited Naples 1770.

Gaetano Caffarelli.bio: Celebrated castrato. Retired to Naples. Met Burney 1770.

Pietro Nardini.bio: Violinist, pupil of Tartini. Met Burney in Florence 1770.

Antonio Sacchini.bio: Opera composer. Met Burney in Venice 1770, later in London.

Andre Gretry.bio: Belgian-born opera composer based in Paris. Met Burney 1770.

Claude Balbastre.bio: Organist at Saint-Roch, Paris. Burney heard him play June 12 1770 and visited his house.

Christian Cannabich.bio: Kapellmeister of the Mannheim orchestra. Met Burney August 1772.

Friedrich Klopstock.bio: Poet. Burney met him in Hamburg, October 1772.

Christoph Daniel Ebeling.bio: German musicologist, Hamburg. Translated Burney's France/Italy volume into German. Corresponded from August 1771.

Richard Shackleton.bio: Quaker schoolmaster. Burke's closest childhood friend. 21 letters with Burke.

Richard Champion.bio: Bristol porcelain manufacturer. Burke's political ally. 35 letters.

Marquis of Rockingham.bio: Charles Watson-Wentworth. Whig PM 1765-66, 1782. Burke's political patron. 49 letters.

Charles James Fox.bio: Whig politician. Burke's ally then opponent over the French Revolution.

Lady Clifford.bio: Aristocratic patron of Charles Burney during his King's Lynn period. Sister of the Duchess of Norfolk. Recommended Madame Saintmard in Paris for the education of Burney's older daughters (1764).

Madame Saintmard.bio: Parisian educator. Took charge of Charles Burney's older daughters (including Esther) in Paris, 1764. Recommended by Lady Clifford.

Elizabeth Meeke.bio: Prolific novelist and translator, stepsister of Frances Burney. Daughter of Elizabeth Allen (CB's second wife) from her first marriage. Published ~30 novels via Minerva Press as "Mrs. Meeke" or pseudonym "Gabrielli". Identity conclusively established by Simon Macdonald in 2013.

Richard Thomas Burney.bio: Son of Charles Burney Sr by second wife Elizabeth Allen. Sent to India c.1785. Headmaster of the Military Orphan School at Kidderpore, Calcutta. Stayed with Charles Grant's household. Influenced by chaplain David Brown and surgeon-missionary John Thomas. Married Jane Ross in Calcutta. Died at Rangoon 1808 (Firminger corrects location). Father of Henry Burney.ied Jane Ross in Calcutta 1787. Headmaster of Orphan School, Kidderpore. Died in Rangoon aged 39. Twelve children born in India.

Charles Arne.bio: Catholic composer. Charles Burney was apprenticed to him in London. JCH Aveling argues the bulk of CB's Catholic contacts derived from this period. CB eventually broke with Arne.

Robert Strange.bio: Jacobite engraver, born Orkney. Fought at Culloden 1745, designed Jacobite currency. Wife's brother was secretary to James Francis Edward Stuart. Pardoned 1747, spent time in Jacobite centre of Rouen. Returned London 1750. Troubled proximity to Burney's own network. ODNB entry.

Isabella Strange.bio: Wife of Robert Strange the Jacobite engraver. Left in charge of his English business while he retreated to Rome in 1765.

Charles Walmesley.bio: Catholic bishop (Vicar Apostolic of the Western District). Frances Burney witnessed his chapel ablaze during the Gordon Riots, Bath, June 1780. She expressed sympathy for the "poor persecuted priest".

Dr Thomas Bever.bio: English friend of Charles Burney who provided contacts for his European tours.

Robert Hudson.bio: English friend of Charles Burney who provided contacts for his European tours.

Mr Drummond.bio: Catholic neighbour on St Martin's Street. Charles Burney taught his daughter music. During the Gordon Riots (June 1780), Mrs Reynolds warned the Burneys that Drummond "was expected to be attacked that night — because his wife & family are catholic."

Dr Seward.bio: Introduced Charles Burney to Mrs Thrale in 1776 as music instructor for her daughter Queeney. This fortuitous introduction brought CB into the Johnson-Thrale circle at Streatham.

Choderlos de Laclos.bio: Author of Les Liaisons Dangereuses. Former roommate of Alexandre d'Arblay. Wrote a 7,000-word review of Cecilia (1784) ranking it among the greatest works of modern European literature. His pen name for a character was taken from d'Arblay's erotic poetry pseudonym.

Louis de Narbonne.bio: French general and politician. Arrived in England with d'Arblay in November 1792, having been second in command during the flight to Varennes. Part of the Juniper Hall set at Mickleham.

Clement Francis.bio: Charlotte Burney's first husband. Accompanied Warren Hastings back from India to England, having resolved in India to marry the author of Evelina — but married her sister Charlotte instead (1786). Died 1792.

Ralph Broome.bio: Charlotte Burney's second husband (married 28 Feb 1798). Bengal Army captain, judge advocate and Persian translator. Published Letters from Simpkin the Second (1788-96) and Elucidation of the Articles of Impeachment (1790) in defence of Hastings. Fathered illegitimate daughter Miriam (c.1781) by an Indian woman. Charles Burney Sr called him 'a Democrat, even a Jacobin'. Died Bath 24 Feb 1805.

Molesworth Phillips.bio: James Burney's close friend and shipmate. Married Susanna Burney January 1782. Promised large Irish estates but these proved much smaller; became violent. Charles forced to loan him £2,000.

Samuel Meeke.bio: Eloped with Elizabeth "Bessie" Allen (Frances's stepsister) at Ypres in October 1777. More than twenty years older than her. Remained in Paris working for Madame de Genlis, attempted to join the Jacobin Club. Separated from Elizabeth; appears to have left France c.1793.

Madame Campan.bio: Former lady-in-waiting to Marie Antoinette. In Napoleonic Paris, invited Frances Burney to a pensionnat, considering her literary fame excellent advertisement for the school.

Jacques-Louis David.bio: French neoclassical painter. Frances Burney visited his studio spring 1812 and saw L'Empereur debout dans son cabinet, a propaganda portrait commissioned by Alexander Hamilton-Douglas.

Oliver Goldsmith.bio: Author of The Vicar of Wakefield and She Stoops to Conquer. Member of Johnson's Literary Club from its founding in 1764.

Richard Brocklesby.bio: Physician. Attended Samuel Johnson in his final illness. Close friend of Edmund Burke. Fellow of the Royal Society.

Adam Smith.bio: Moral philosopher and political economist. Author of The Theory of Moral Sentiments and The Wealth of Nations. Close friend of David Hume.

Duke of Norfolk.bio: Premier Catholic peer of England. The Norfolk family's Catholicism was central to English recusant identity. Sister Lady Clifford was CB's patron at King's Lynn.

John Young.bio: Glasgow classicist. Charles Burney Jr's most prolific correspondent (264 letters, 1788-1817). More letters than to any family member except Frances. Identified by Coulombeau & Waterfield's "Collecting Charles Burney" project (Burney Society, 2021-22). Essentially unstudied.

Samuel Parr.bio: Classical scholar and Whig polemicist, known as the "Whig Johnson." Schoolmaster at Stanmore and later at Hatton. 133 letters to CB Jr (1781-1817), his second most prolific correspondent. Renowned Latinist and controversialist.

Richard Heber.bio: Legendary bibliomaniac who accumulated 150,000+ volumes across eight houses in England, France, and Belgium. Purchased 6+ lots at the 1814 Burney library sale (plus items via his agent Robert Triphook). His library was dispersed at the Bibliotheca Heberiana sales (1834-37, 216 auction days).

Joseph Haydn.bio: Austrian composer. CB Sr's doctoral exercise "I will love thee O Lord my Strength" was performed in Oxford and later by C.P.E. Bach in Hamburg (1773). Haydn visited London 1791-92 and 1794-95.

Cecilia Burney.bio: Daughter of Charles Burney Jr and his wife Esther (née Burney). Composer — her Piano Sonata Op.2 "Le séjour agréable" and the song "Lady Avondel's Song" survive. The Sonata was bound in a volume collected by Margaret "Peggy" Hazlitt (William Hazlitt's sister, c.1795-1817), now in the Sydney Living Museums (Historic Houses of Trust of NSW). Published by Chappell & Co, 1817.

Marquis de Lafayette.bio: Gilbert du Motier, Marquis de Lafayette. French aristocrat, general, and statesman. Veteran of the American War of Independence and a major figure of the early French Revolution.

Marquis de Lally-Tollendal.bio: Gerard de Lally-Tollendal. French politician and writer, active in the early Revolution and later in emigre politics in Britain.

Victor de Latour Maubourg.bio: Marie Victor de Fay, marquis de Latour-Maubourg. French general and diplomat of the Revolutionary and Napoleonic era.

Adrienne de Noailles.bio: Adrienne de Noailles, marquise de Lafayette. French noblewoman and wife of Lafayette, imprisoned during the Terror.

Charles-Maurice de Talleyrand-Perigord.bio: French diplomat and statesman, former bishop of Autun, who navigated the ancien regime, Revolution, Empire, and Restoration.

Louis-Alexandre Berthier.bio: Marshal of France and Napoleon's chief of staff. Central military administrator of the Revolutionary and Napoleonic wars.

Warren Hastings.bio: First Governor-General of India 1773-85. Impeached 1788, acquitted 1795. Subscribed to Burney's Camilla. Frances Burney witnessed his trial at Westminster Hall.

Hester Chapone.bio: Bluestocking essayist. Author of Letters on the Improvement of the Mind (1773). Corresponded with Frances Burney 1782-1801.

Elizabeth Pleydell.bio: Daughter of John Zephaniah Holwell, chronicler of the Black Hole of Calcutta. Married Charles Stafford Pleydell. Gave Frances Burney 'finest India muslin' 1769.

Lord George Pigot.bio: Governor of Madras 1755-63 and 1775-77. Frances Burney met him 1769. Defended Madras against the French; died in captivity after Council mutiny.

Madame de Tessé.bio: Adrienne-Catherine de Noailles, comtesse de Tessé. French aristocrat and salon hostess. Frances Burney corresponded with her during Paris years 1802-06.

Princesse d'Hénin.bio: Etiennette-Charlotte-Adélaïde de Domangeville, princesse d'Hénin. French émigré in London, later returned to Paris. Corresponded with Frances Burney.

Madame de Souza.bio: Spanish woman Frances Burney met in Paris 1802. Her scandalous story of following her lover's son to France parallels The Wanderer's plot.

Lucrezia Agujari.bio: Italian soprano known as 'La Bastardella'. Performed at Burneys' home c.1775; 'Pantheon-price' was 50 guineas per song.

Giuseppe Millico.bio: Italian soprano castrato, 'the divine Millico'. Performed at the Burneys' home.

Antonio Sacchini.bio: Italian opera composer active in London 1772-81. Performed at the Burneys' home.

Eligio Celestino.bio: Italian violinist who performed at the Burneys' home. Frances called the evening 'heavenly'.

Omai.bio: Polynesian man from Raiatea who visited England 1774-76 via Captain Cook's second voyage. Befriended by James Burney; visited the Burney household.

Count Alexei Orlov.bio: Russian military commander, favourite of Catherine the Great, implicated in assassination of Peter III. Visited the Burneys in London.

Elizabeth Juliana Schwellenberg.bio: Keeper of the Robes alongside Frances Burney at Queen Charlotte's court. German-born. Tyrannical and ill-tempered colleague who isolated Burney from friends and family.

Stephen Digby.bio: Courtier at Queen Charlotte's court with 'pronounced romantic interest' in Frances Burney. Son of Henry Digby, 1st Earl Digby.

Margaret Planta.bio: Former Court acquaintance of Frances Burney. Burney wrote to her from Paris 1802 about Madame de Souza.

Duchess Dowager of Portland.bio: Margaret Cavendish Bentinck, 2nd Duchess of Portland. Collector, naturalist, patron. Hosted dinner party with Burney, Chapone, and Mary Delany January 1783.

Clement Francis.bio: Surgeon who served under Warren Hastings in India. Married Charlotte Burney 1786. Resolved in India to marry the author of Evelina but married her sister Charlotte instead.

Arnail-Francois de Jaucourt.bio: French politician and diplomat. Member of Juniper Hall émigré circle 1793. Later served under Napoleon and the Restoration. Lifelong friend of d'Arblay.

Pierre Victor Malouet.bio: French politician and colonial administrator. Monarchist constitutionalist. Part of Juniper Hall circle 1793. Later Minister of Marine under Napoleon.

Mrs Ord.bio: Anna Ord. Friend of Frances Burney during the Court period. Regular visitor and correspondent.

Marie-Elisabethe de La Fite.bio: Writer and governess at Queen Charlotte's court. French-born Protestant. Fellow attendant and companion to Frances Burney at Court 1786-91.

Leonard Smelt.bio: Military engineer and Sub-Governor to the Prince of Wales and Prince Frederick. Friend of the Burney family. Discussed Warren Hastings with Frances at Windsor 1787.

Robert Greville.bio: Colonel Robert Fulke Greville. Equerry to George III. Discussed Warren Hastings with Frances Burney at Windsor 1787.

Dominique-Jean baron Larrey.bio: Surgeon-in-Chief of Napoleon's Grande Armée. Performed Frances Burney's mastectomy in Paris, 30 September 1811.

Comtesse de Simiane.bio: Dame-Adelaide de Damas d'Antigny. Intimate friend of Lafayette. Part of Frances Burney's Paris circle 1802.

R.B. Sheridan.bio: Playwright and politician. Author of The School for Scandal, The Rivals. Manager of Drury Lane. Lead prosecutor at Hastings trial. Married Elizabeth Linley, who performed at the Burneys' home.

Frederica Montagu.bio: Frederick Montagu. Politician and nephew of Elizabeth Montagu. Bowed to Frances Burney at Westminster Hall during Hastings trial 1788.

Henry Burney.bio: Son of Richard Thomas Burney, born 27 Feb 1792 Calcutta. EIC Bengal army from 1807. Married Janet Bannerman 1818 at Penang. Led mission to Siam 1825; negotiated Burney Treaty with King Rama III (20 Jun 1826). Deputy Commissioner of Tavoy 1827-29. British Resident at Ava 1829-38; mastered Burmese by 1832. Resolved Kabaw Valley dispute in Burma's favour. Published in JASB on Pagan and Buddhist inscriptions. Compiled unpublished Pali dictionary. Lt Colonel 1834. 13 children. Died 4 Mar 1845 at sea. Papers at Cambridge (RCMS 65). Biography: D.G.E. Hall, Henry Burney: A Political Biography (OUP/SOAS, 1974).

Jane Ross Burney.bio: Wife of Richard Thomas Burney, married in Calcutta. Mother of Henry Burney.

Charles Grant.bio: Scottish EIC commercial resident in Bengal, converted to evangelicalism c.1776. Director then Chairman of the East India Company. MP 1802-18. Core Clapham Sect member with Wilberforce and Thornton. Hosted Richard Thomas Burney in Calcutta. Wrote Observations on the State of Society among Asiatic Subjects (1792).

David Brown.bio: EIC chaplain, arrived Calcutta 1786. Senior chaplain at Fort William from 1797. Purchased Aldeen House, Serampore (1803), gathering place for Baptist missionaries and evangelical chaplains. Founded Calcutta Bible Society 1811. Married Frances Cowley, daughter of playwright Hannah Cowley (1796). Connected to Richard Thomas Burney at Kidderpore.

John Thomas.bio: Surgeon turned Baptist missionary, first to Bengal. Funded by Charles Grant at Gaumalti mission 1787-89. Accompanied William Carey to India 1793. Based partly at Kidderpore where Richard Thomas Burney ran the Military Orphan School. Died Dinajpur 1801.

Miriam Broome.bio: Illegitimate daughter of Ralph Broome by an unnamed Indian woman. Brought to England c.1785. Married Ralph Broome's lawyer nephew (also Ralph Broome) in 1803. Step-daughter of Charlotte Burney.

Tysoe Saul Hancock.bio: EIC surgeon at Madras from 1745. Married Philadelphia Austen (Jane Austen's aunt) 1753. Close friend of Warren Hastings in Bengal. Their daughter Eliza was goddaughter of Hastings (£10,000 trust). Died Calcutta 1775.

Philadelphia Hancock.bio: Née Austen, Jane Austen's aunt. Married Tysoe Saul Hancock 1753 in India. Mother of Eliza, who married first the Comte de Feuillide (guillotined 1794), then Henry Austen.

Eliza de Feuillide.bio: Born Calcutta, goddaughter of Warren Hastings (who settled £10,000 on her). Daughter of Philadelphia and Tysoe Hancock; persistent rumour that Hastings was biological father. Married (1) Comte de Feuillide (guillotined 1794), (2) Henry Austen 1797, becoming Jane Austen's sister-in-law.

Marianne Francis.bio: Daughter of Charlotte Burney and Clement Francis, sister of Charlotte Barrett. Evangelical; fluent in Hebrew and Arabic. Corresponded with Barbara Wilberforce. Connection to Clapham Sect.

William Carey.bio: Baptist missionary, 'father of modern missions'. Arrived Bengal 1793 with John Thomas. Based at Serampore. Operated partly from Kidderpore. Connected to the Grant-Brown evangelical network that Richard Thomas Burney was embedded in.

Janet Bannerman.bio: Wife of Henry Burney, married 1818 at George Town, Penang. Niece of John Alexander Bannerman, Governor of Penang. Mother of 13 children. Survived Henry by 20 years.

King Rama III.bio: Nangklao, King of Siam 1824-51. Signed the Burney Treaty with Henry Burney on 20 June 1826, establishing commercial relations between Siam and Britain.

William Kirkpatrick.bio: EIC captain who founded the Bengal Military Orphan Society in 1782. The institution educated orphans of British officers and soldiers at Kidderpore, Calcutta.

Richard Thomas Burney Jr.bio: Son of Henry Burney. Married Julia Maria Naylor in Bengal 1861. Confirmed continuing Burney presence in India into third generation.

Susan Allen Burney.bio: Daughter of Henry Burney, born 12 May 1823 at Penang.

Rev. Henry Bannerman Burney.bio: Son of Henry Burney. Vicar of Norton St Philip, Somerset, 1866-1890. Returned to England from the family's Asian career.
